items.text: I still believe that the addition of benefits for a stronger charge is in line with the spirit of tOW and previous versions of Ogre Charge, however, I really didn’t think through how likely the original version made it to happen.

segments.text: I still believe that the addition of benefits for a stronger charge is in line with the spirit of tOW and previous versions of Ogre Charge, however, I really didn’t think through how likely the original version made it to happen.

items.text: Low Linear Obstacles (as battlefield terrain, magical effects, or unit benefits) essentially negate all Ogre infantry. This can make some matchups particularly binary. Making them essentially immune to the risk of encountering an LLO is similarly a negative play experience for the opponent.

segments.text: Low Linear Obstacles (as battlefield terrain, magical effects, or unit benefits) essentially negate all Ogre infantry. This can make some matchups particularly binary. Making them essentially immune to the risk of encountering an LLO is similarly a negative play experience for the opponent.

items.text: Therefore I would like to submit the following: the effect triggers on a natural six rolled when rolling for charge range. This gives the effect a 30% chance of success on the dice, and around 50% with a re-roll. Enough to call it a “chance” rather than a bankable guarantee. Furthermore, rather than the usual 3” for impact hits, the juiced up Ogre Charge triggers only if your charge move actually takes you 6” or more. This provides some opportunity for counterplay if an LLO is essential to your opponent's game, and some positioning skill to set up on the Ogre player’s part.
